Du willst als Team Lead Sales in Berlin ein Vertriebsteam führen und gleichzeitig mitgestalten, wie Pennylane Steuerkanzleien in Deutschland gewinnt? Als erste Sales-Teamleitung für unser deutsches Kanzleisegment baust du ein Team regionaler Account Executives auf, das Kanzleien aktiv gewinnt – Outbound wie Inbound: Du coachst im Kundengespräch, steuerst die Vertriebsleistung und entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Sales Firms Director den Ansatz für den deutschen Markt – mit dem Rückenwind eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Fintechs Europas.

Deine Mission

Du wirst die oder der erste Team Lead Sales (m/w/d) – Steuerkanzleien in Deutschland sein. Deine Mission ist es, mit deinem Team von Account Executives Steuerkanzleien in ganz Deutschland für Pennylane zu gewinnen – du führst, coachst und baust das Team aus.

In Frankreich ist Pennylane in diesem Segment innerhalb von fünf Jahren zum Marktführer geworden. Du übernimmst das bewährte Playbook und passt es gemeinsam mit unserem Sales Firms Director, an den du direkt berichtest, an den deutschen Kanzleimarkt an. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit Tobias Janiesch, Managing Director Deutschland, zusammen. Unser Prozess: Erstgespräch, Interview mit dem Sales Firms Director, Case Study, Onsite-Gespräch mit dem Team in Berlin.

Dein Team

  • Full-Cycle Sales: Deine Account Executives verantworten den gesamten Prozess – von der Qualifizierung über die Produkt-Demo und den Abschluss bis zum Onboarding und Account Management ihrer Kanzleien.

  • Outbound ist Kern: Einen wesentlichen Teil eurer Pipeline baut ihr selbst auf – per Telefon, LinkedIn, Branchenevents und Kanzleibesuche. Wer nur auf Inbound wartet, wird hier nicht glücklich; wer gern aktiv Türen öffnet, umso mehr.

  • Starkes Setup: Dabei seid ihr nicht allein: Unser eigenes Customer-Success-Team in Berlin unterstützt euch bei Onboarding und Betreuung der Kanzleien, damit deine AEs genug Zeit für die Neukundengewinnung haben.

  • Regional organisiert: Jede:r AE betreut eine feste Region in Deutschland – per Inside Sales und vor Ort in den Kanzleien.

  • Im Aufbau: Du übernimmst aktuell zwei Account Executives und stellst gemeinsam mit unserem Talent-Acquisition-Team weitere ein – das Team wächst mit dir.

  • Beratender Vertrieb: Dein Team gewinnt Kanzleiinhaber:innen und Partner:innen für eine neue Art der Zusammenarbeit mit ihren Mandanten. Ihr macht den Nutzen von Pennylane für den Kanzleialltag konkret und schafft Vertrauen in die Einführung einer neuen Plattform.

  • Standort Berlin: Das Team wird aus unserem Berliner Office geführt – du bist an zwei Tagen pro Woche vor Ort, den Rest flexibel. Rund 30 % deiner Zeit bist du bei deinen AEs und in Kanzleien in Deutschland unterwegs, in der Regel ein Termin pro Woche, den du selbst planst.

Du wirst für die Leistung dieses Teams verantwortlich sein durch:

  • Du verantwortest die Vertriebsleistung deines Teams: den MRR aus deutschen Steuerkanzleien und die Marktdurchdringung von Pennylane im deutschen Kanzleisegment.

  • Du baust mit deinem Team eine systematische Outbound-Akquise für Kanzleien auf – Zielkundenlisten, Sequenzen, Events, Vor-Ort-Besuche – und hältst die Aktivitätsquoten hoch.

  • Du schaffst klare Erwartungen, coachst regelmäßig anhand konkreter Kundengespräche und nutzt Pipeline- und Conversion-Daten, um dein Team gezielt weiterzuentwickeln.

  • Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit dem Head of Sales den Go-to-Market-Ansatz für Kanzleien weiter (Inside Sales + Field Sales) und setzt ihn mit deinem Team um.

  • Du begleitest deine AEs im Feld – bei Kanzleibesuchen, Branchenevents und Key Deals.

  • Du arbeitest eng mit dem französischen Sales-Team zusammen und überträgst, was vom Playbook für Deutschland funktioniert.

Als Team Lead Sales – Steuerkanzleien sind deine Ziele vielfältig:

  • Du erreichst die Vertriebsziele des Teams und steuerst das Tagesgeschäft – im Office wie bei den AEs in ihren Regionen.

  • Du verantwortest das Sales Enablement deiner Account Executives: Techniken, Messaging und der gesamte Pennylane-Sales-Prozess.

  • Du begleitest neue AEs durch Onboarding und Ramp-up und führst sie zu ihren Zielen.

  • Du baust Teamgeist, Engagement und Wohlbefinden auf – mit Challenges, Teambuildings und Formaten, die du selbst gestaltest.

  • Du bringst die Perspektive des Kanzleivertriebs in die Sales-OKRs von Pennylane Deutschland ein.

  • Du gehst bei wichtigen Deals selbst mit rein – vor Ort in der Kanzlei oder per Video-Call.

Dein Profil

  • Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung im B2B-Sales mit – idealerweise SaaS mit mehrstufigen Deal-Zyklen und mehreren Stakeholdern – und hast bereits ein Sales-Team (AEs / Full-Cycle) erfolgreich geführt. Diese Führungserfahrung ist uns wichtiger als eine bestimmte Jahreszahl.

  • Ein Plus: Du kennst den Markt der Steuerkanzleien oder das Accounting-/Fintech-Ökosystem – oder hast an Steuerberater:innen, Kanzleien oder andere Berufsträger verkauft. Wenn nicht, bringst du die Neugier mit, dich schnell einzuarbeiten.

  • Du hast selbst Outbound gemacht und Teams darin geführt: Kaltakquise bei Inhaber:innen und Entscheider:innen schreckt dich nicht – sie ist dein Hebel.

  • Du bist ein Builder: Du hast schon einmal ein Team, einen Markt oder einen Prozess aufgebaut – idealerweise in einem schnell wachsenden Umfeld (Scale-up) – und baust Vertrauen auf, im Team wie bei Kanzleiinhaber:innen.

  • Du führst über Coaching: Du entwickelst Menschen anhand echter Kundengespräche, mit Daten, klarem Feedback und dem Mut, Entscheidungen zu treffen und durchzuhalten.

  • Du bist hands-on: Du führst nicht nur vom Dashboard aus, sondern gehst selbst mit in Deals – auch vor Ort.

  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (C2) – deine Kund:innen sind deutsche Kanzleien – und Englisch auf C1-Niveau für die Zusammenarbeit mit Paris.

  • Du lebst in Berlin oder bist bereit, nach Berlin zu ziehen – und du bist gern bei Kunden vor Ort (rund 30 % Reiseanteil).

Was wir tun, um dein Arbeitsleben besser zu machen

  • 🏢 Berlin, hybrid: zwei Tage pro Woche in unserem Berliner Office, die übrigen Tage flexibel.

  • 🌴 30 Urlaubstage pro Jahr.

  • 💵 Ein attraktives OTE-Paket: Fixgehalt plus variabler Anteil, gekoppelt an den MRR, den dein Team erzielt.

  • 📈 Du erhältst Unternehmensanteile, um vom Erfolg mitzuprofitieren, den du gemeinsam mit uns aufbaust.

  • 🏡 Du erhältst ein Budget, um dein Zuhause in einen komfortableren Arbeitsplatz zu verwandeln.

  • 🇫🇷 Onboarding im Pariser HQ, regelmäßiger Austausch mit dem französischen Sales-Team und Zugang zu Busuu, um dein Englisch oder Französisch zu perfektionieren.

  • 💻 Du erhältst die neueste Apple-Ausrüstung.

  • 🎉 Wir legen Wert auf regelmäßige gemeinsame Veranstaltungen wie unsere Tech Days (alle 3 Monate) oder unser jährliches Firmenseminar – plus Team-Events in Berlin.

Wir wissen, dass einige Menschen eher zögern, sich zu bewerben, wenn sie das Gefühl haben, nicht die gesamte Liste der Kriterien zu erfüllen. Wenn du unsicher bist, ermutigen wir dich, dich trotzdem zu bewerben: Wer weiß, vielleicht ist es der Beginn einer sinnvollen und langfristigen Zusammenarbeit.

Wir möchten auch betonen, dass wir Vielfalt, Gleichheit und Inklusion voll und ganz befürworten und unser Bestes tun, um ein sicheres und integratives Umfeld zu schaffen. Wir verpflichten uns, gleiche Beschäftigungsmöglichkeiten unabhängig von Geschlecht, sexueller Orientierung, Herkunft, Behinderungen oder anderen Merkmalen, die dich ausmachen, zu gewährleisten. Im Gegenteil, Vielfalt macht uns zu einem noch besseren Arbeitsplatz.

Join SE3 Labs as Head of Marketing / Communications

Build a credible brand around SE3's technology and work in the field, and tell our story to the people who matter most.

About SE3

SE3 Labs builds spatial intelligence and autonomy software for unmanned systems. We combine 3D computer vision, state estimation and AI to help autonomous platforms perceive their surroundings, know where they are and operate when GPS and other sensors become unreliable. Defence is a core application of our work today.

We are growing to a team of 100+ people. Join at a stage where you can shape our Marketing team, help build the team and grow your responsibilities as the company expands.

About the Role

As Head of Marketing / Communications, you'll build our marketing team and our brand internationally, telling SE3's story to government customers, industry partners, investors and future colleagues. You'll work closely with our founders, engineers and a strong designer, ideally based with the team in Munich. Excellence in marketing matters more to us than a defence background, and we'll complement you with people who know German defence and security policy in depth.

What You'll Work On

  • Brand: Build a credible institutional brand around our technology and our work in the field.

  • Storytelling: Tell our story to government customers, industry partners, investors and the people we want to hire.

  • Content Quality: Own the quality of our writing, website, press and other content, and write and edit much of it yourself.

  • Media Relations: Build media relationships and help the founders communicate clearly.

  • Creative Partners: Work with design, video and subject-matter specialists to produce excellent work.

  • Team Building: Hire the marketing team, set the bar and stay hands-on.

Your Profile

  • You take ownership of outcomes and remove obstacles without waiting for direction. You turn discussions into clear decisions and decisions into deliverables, and you hold yourself and your team to a consistently high standard.

  • You write and tell stories excellently in English, with work to show and clarity about what you did yourself.

  • You have built a credible brand, ideally for a technology company, and explained complex subjects to different audiences.

  • You can build and lead a strong marketing team while staying hands-on.

  • You have a high quality bar and work well with strong designers.

  • You speak fluent English; German is a plus. Given the nature of SE3's work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to work on defence-related projects and, where required, obtain the relevant security clearance.

Especially Valued Bonus Skills

  • Strong media relationships.

  • Experience communicating on sensitive topics.

  • Agency or VC marketing experience.

  • Familiarity with defence or security.

Perks & Benefits

  • Real Ownership: Participate in SE3's growth through our employee participation programme

  • 31 Paid Days Off: 30 vacation days plus your birthday off

  • Team Offsites: We go on 2 company retreats per year, our last ones were in Italy and Greece

Our Process

  1. Intro Call (30 min): Let's get to know each other.

Equal Opportunity

SE3 is an equal-opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. Who We Are

Hi, we're DuckDuckGo, the online protection company and remote-first team of 400+ on a mission to raise the standard of trust online. Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, our annual revenue is in the hundreds of millions USD and millions use our browser on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, our search engine, and the DuckDuckGo subscription. We also offer private, useful, and optional AI, including Duck.ai, which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place.

 

Our culture of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place!

Your Team and Role

Working on the Web Dependability Engineering team, you'll make sure websites just work in DuckDuckGo's browsers across Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, helping ensure our users have the best-possible experience browsing with DuckDuckGo. Recent projects include:

  • Reverse-engineering how sites detect our privacy protections and building countermeasures that keep pages working

  • Shimming browser APIs so sites work seamlessly across different browser engines and system webviews

  • Building LLM agent pipelines that automatically reproduce and triage reported site breakage

 

As a Senior Web Compatibility Engineer, you'll be our resident expert on why websites break and how to fix them: owning the webcompat side of our triage process, debugging gnarly issues in code you don't control, distinguishing site bugs from browser bugs from privacy protection-induced breakage, leading the charge when a top site breaks and becomes an incident, shipping durable fixes across every platform, and work on related projects that prevent user churn and keep users coming back to DuckDuckGo.

About You

  • 7+ years of experience building and debugging complex web applications with vanilla JavaScript.

  • Detailed knowledge of web standards, web components, and browser APIs. Any additional experience with our stack is a bonus: Swift/Kotlin/C#/C++/Python.

  • Advanced ability to reverse-engineer obfuscated third-party code and reduce issues to minimal test cases.

  • Passion for hunting elusive bugs and tracing them to their root cause.

  • Interest in automating repetitive work and building agentic tooling that multiplies the team's impact.

  • Experience triaging issues, leading incident response, and communicating clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Experience shipping code beyond the web, like native or desktop clients.

  • Ability to lead complex, ambiguous projects with little to no oversight.

Uns ist die Freude an der Arbeit ebenso wichtig wie der Erfolg. Wir hoffen natürlich, dass es dir bei uns genauso gehen wird. Der Einsatz gegen Jugendarbeitslosigkeit und die Möglichkeit, damit wirklich etwas in der Gesellschaft zu bewegen, liegen uns allen am Herzen. Deswegen geben wir gerne alles für unsere Teilnehmenden. Persönlichkeit und Team-Fit sind für uns besonders wichtig, und wir sind gespannt darauf, dich im Bewerbungsprozess näher kennenzulernen. Wir würden uns freuen, wenn du bereits einige dieser Hard Facts mitbringst:

Are you part of London’s music community and passionate about teaching? Join First Chair, Matchspace Music’s founding ambassador programme, and help bring Europe’s leading platform for music educators to musicians across London.

We’re selecting six musicians to help launch Matchspace Music in the UK. You’ll connect with fellow musicians across the city, share what you’re hearing on the ground, and help us understand what independent music teachers need to build and grow their teaching practice.

You won’t be handed a script to promote. You’ll help shape how we arrive in London, from the very first week.

About Matchspace Music

Matchspace Music is Europe’s leading platform for music educators. We help independent music teachers build a professional online presence, get discovered by students, manage their lesson offers and get paid, all in one place.

Founded in Switzerland in 2020, we are home to more than 2,000 qualified teachers across over 100 instruments, with more than 2,100 international teachers registered ahead of our launch. We’re now bringing this to the UK, starting with London.

What you’ll do

As a First Chair ambassador, you’ll:

  • Introduce Matchspace Music to musicians in your peer networks.

  • Start conversations about teaching and the challenges of building an independent teaching practice.

A student or recent graduate of a London conservatoire, we’re starting conversations at RAM, RCM, Guildhall and Trinity Laban, and welcome ambitious musicians from across the city, in any discipline: strings, piano, voice, jazz, composition and beyond.

Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

This is not a traditional laboratory role. We're looking for a Biomedical Scientist who is comfortable working differently, embraces innovation, and takes pride in delivering accurate results at exceptional pace.

Neko Health members come through our clinics for whole-body preventive health screenings, and our laboratories sit at the centre of the patient journey. They are busy, modern spaces, and the service continues to develop as we scale.

This is a hands-on, autonomous role, based on site in one of our central London laboratories. As a Biomedical Scientist, you will operate our Abbott Alinity and Sysmex XN-550 analysers and support the quality systems that allow us to return results within 30 minutes of sample receipt.

If you're a BMS looking to further develop your career in an innovation-led environment, we would love to hear from you.

 

What You'll Deliver in the First 6 - 12 Months

  • Initialise the analysers each day and ready them for sample processing.

  • Perform testing on our Abbott Alinity (biochemistry and immunoassay) and Sysmex XN-550 (haematology) analysers, validating patient results and escalating clinically anomalous or unexpected findings.

  • Carry out daily calibration, internal quality control, and routine maintenance of analysers, troubleshooting and escalating technical issues promptly.

  • Work within our ISO 15189-aligned, UKAS-facing quality management system: author SOP updates, monitor EQA performance, support audits, and investigate non-conformances.

  • Contribute to service improvement work, including analyser verification, reagent evaluation, and software testing.

  • Maintain accurate, auditable records and support performance monitoring across turnaround times, KPIs, and consumables usage.

  • Provide technical guidance to clinical colleagues and support training across the lab team.

 

Minimum Requirements

  • HCPC registration as a Biomedical Scientist, with evidence of ongoing CPD.

  • Minimum one year of post-registration experience in clinical chemistry and immunoassay, including IQC and EQA practice.

  • Demonstrable experience operating an integrated clinical chemistry and immunoassay analyser.

  • Experience working accurately and efficiently under time pressure, suited to a low-volume, fast-turnaround service model.

 

Preferred

  • Post-registration experience in haematology.

  • Hands-on experience operating Sysmex XN-series haematology analysers.

  • Hands-on experience operating Abbott Alinity ci-series.

  • Experience in POCT, rapid diagnostics, or high-throughput clinical settings.

  • Experience with laboratory information management systems (LIMS), digital result reporting, or involvement in LIMS development and user acceptance testing.

About titles at Neko

We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so the title on this posting may differ from your internal title. We’ll be open about the scope and level of the role throughout the process, so you know exactly what you’d be taking on.

data.description:
Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

You own the clinical bar across the Neko clinics in the North and Midlands (currently Birmingham and Manchester).

That means every consultation in your area meets the same threshold of safety, quality, and member experience across your region. It means the clinical teams working with you are developing, not just performing. It means clinical issues are being seen and addressed before they show up in audits or member complaints. And it means the quality metrics for your region are known, owned and moving in the right direction. And it means clinical judgment shows up at the table when operational decisions are being made.

You'll partner closely with the UK Medical Director, who holds final clinical authority for the UK market, and operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager for your region who owns the operational side. The clinical health of the region is yours.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Hold the clinical standard across every site in your area

  • Manage and develop the clinicians in your region: performance conversations, development plans, coaching, and the honest feedback that turns good clinicians into great ones.

  • Ensure lead clinicians in your market(s) are performing excellently and that the clinical teams have the appropriate clinical escalation pathways in place.

  • Support clinical hiring for your area against defined criteria, and partner with the Training and Education team to close training gaps as they emerge.

  • Own the review and closure of clinical incidents and near-misses in your area, making sure learnings are actually applied, not just documented.

  • Own the quality metrics for your region: accountable for performance against Neko's medical quality goals at area level, including scan quality (perfect scan score), member follow-up quality and timeliness (perfect follow-up score and follow-up SLAs), clinical safety (Northstar Clinical Safety score) and clinician summary quality and timeliness. Review the data with your Area Clinic Manager each week and month, trace variation to root cause by site and clinician, set improvement actions, and report progress and risks to the UK Medical Director.

  • Operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager: co-owning quality, member experience, and business goals, attending and contributing to Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews, and bringing clinical input into operational decisions before they're made.

  • Round your sites regularly to observe, support, and listen, surfacing what's working so it can spread, and what isn't so it can be addressed.

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with the GPs, NHS trusts and private specialist clinicians who receive Neko referrals, monitoring referral quality and addressing breakdowns quickly.

  • Know the UK regulatory landscape: CQC registration and inspection standards, GMC/NMC professional standards and revalidation, NHS and GP referral pathways and obligations, and UK-specific clinical rules, and flag emerging risks before they become problems.

  • Lead or participate in clinical pilots as required - defining success, capturing learnings, and documenting outcomes so the rest of the company can learn from your region.

What We're Hiring For

  • Holds the Bar at Scale. You're the kind of clinical leader who can make sure every consultation feels the same regardless of site or clinician, not by micromanaging, but by setting a clear standard, coaching to it, and noticing when it drifts. You're rigorous without being rigid.

  • Develops the Clinicians You Lead. You take clinician development seriously. You give honest feedback even when it's uncomfortable. You spot what someone needs before they ask. You know the difference between a clinician who needs coaching and one who needs to leave, and you don't avoid either conversation.

  • The Dyad That Actually Works. You bring clinical judgment into operational decisions before they're made and you stay constructive when clinical standards and operational targets pull in different directions. When you escalate, it's because something genuinely needs leadership attention, not because you've stopped trying to resolve it locally.

  • Reads the Pattern, Not Just the Report. You don't just review the data. You see what it's telling you. You round your sites and notice things that don't show up in dashboards. When you spot a pattern you trace it to the root cause and you make sure the right people hear about it.

  • Trusted Outside the Walls. The referral network, the regulators, the specialist clinicians who receive Neko members: these relationships sit with you. You represent Neko credibly because you're a credible clinician yourself. People in the local medical community know your name, and when you flag something, they take it seriously.

Minimum Requirements

  • Full GMC registration with a license to practice, in good standing and with a current revalidation, and right to work in the UK.

  • On the GMC GP Register with qualification (CCT or equivalent) in General Practice.

  • 4+ years of medical leadership experience in the UK health system (NHS and/or private sector), including direct management of clinicians.

  • Demonstrated experience holding clinical standards across multiple sites or a large clinical team.

Preferred

  • Experience in preventive care, tech enabled healthcare or longitudinal care models.

  • Experience operating in a clinical-operational dyad structure.

  • Experience leading clinical pilots or scaling new clinical workflows across multiple sites.

We’re looking for a talented and highly experienced Senior Match 3 Level Designer to join our lovely and ambitious game team and help craft fun, rewarding and memorable puzzle experiences for our cozy mobile game.

You’ll own the match-3 gameplay experience, helping to define the game’s level design framework while delivering best-in-class levels that strike the right balance of challenge, progression and delight. From core gameplay tuning and mechanic development through to polished, data-informed level iterations, you’ll take ownership of the player experience and continually raise the quality bar.

You’ll work closely with game designers, artists, developers and analysts to ensure the match-3 is satisfying, intuitive and rewarding, evolving its mechanics, pacing and feel so that the game’s creative vision and long-term engagement goals come through. You’ll use player feedback, analytics and playtesting to refine gameplay, experiment with new ideas and shape the ongoing evolution of the game’s core puzzle experience.

As a senior member of the team, you’ll also help shape our level production strategy, driving quality with both internal development and external partners while contributing to the long-term direction of the game.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design, build and balance exceptional match-3 levels that deliver engaging gameplay across a wide range of player skill levels.

  • Collaborate with designers, product managers, programmers and analysts to tune game feel and match 3 gameplay to be best-in-class

  • Own the design of blockers, boosters and shape satisfying level progression

  • Use analytics, player feedback and playtesting to continuously refine levels and improve player experience and reach product goals

  • Work alongside Engineering to improve level design tools, workflows and implementation processes.

  • Partner with Art to ensure levels are visually readable, aesthetically cohesive and support the game’s creative vision.

  • Plan and own Match 3 content production, ensuring a consistent pipeline of high-quality content that supports development milestones and LiveOps.

    • Lead external level design contractors and outsourcing partners by providing clear briefs, regular feedback and quality reviews, ensuring all delivered content meets the team’s standards.

  • Mentor other designers through feedback, knowledge sharing and collaborative problem solving.

  • Have a deep understanding of the competition and genre trends.

What You Have

  • Experience shipping successful free-to-play match-3 or puzzle games.

  • Experience designing LiveOps events, seasonal content or limited-time game modes.

  • Strong understanding of player progression, retention, engagement and monetisation in puzzle.

  • Experience improving level editors, pipelines or content creation workflows.

  • Experience leading small feature teams or mentoring designers.

  • Passion for cosy games and creating emotionally engaging player experiences.

  • A self-starter approach to use AI: you've found ways to use it in your day-to-day work, you experiment, figure things out and bring the same energy to every new challenge.

What We're Looking for

  • A strong sense of ownership, with the ability to drive work forward autonomously.

  • A consistent track record of delivering high-quality work that meets design requirements and project goals.

  • A proactive mindset, with the ability to identify opportunities and solve problems.

  • Sound judgement in balancing creative excellence with production efficiency.

  • The ability to lead external partners with clarity, empathy and high standards.

  • A collaborative approach to sharing knowledge, mentoring designers and raising the team’s quality bar.

  • Clear communication skills and the confidence to constructively challenge decisions.

  • A player-first mindset, balanced with an understanding of creative, technical and commercial goals.

  • A commitment to fostering a collaborative, inclusive and positive team culture.

Where You'll Be

This role is based in our London office. The team values in-person collaboration and typically works from the office three days a week: Mondays, Tuesdays and Fridays.

–––

That's it about the role! Below, we've gathered some things we feel are important for you to know. Totally optional, but a highly recommended read.

Once you're ready to apply, just send us your application through the form on the bottom of the page.

–––

About Supercell

Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. You might know us as the makers of Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Boom Beach, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars. Our mission is to create great games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever.

So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and giving them the freedom and independence to succeed. And by taking risks, failing, sharing learnings, and killing lots of projects.

Hey, You Might Love It Here!

Independent cells and trust are at the core of our culture. But it takes more than that to make great games. We take good care of our people, providing them with the compensation, work environment, and resources they need to succeed while having fun along the way.

You Are Not Your Job Title ™

Here, you won’t need to focus on chasing titles or climbing ladders. Internally, our job titles don’t include prefixes like Senior, Junior, Principal, or Director. Recognition isn’t tied to your title, as it doesn't define the impact you can have around here.

Benefits and Compensation

Luring you in with glitter, glamour, and gems isn't what we're about. We want you to enjoy your time here fully, so we structure our compensation and benefits with that in mind. It starts with perceiving you as a human being, not a resource.

Relocation? Yes!

No matter where you’re moving from, our dedicated mobility team and partners will support you throughout your move. We’ll ensure the process is as smooth as possible for you and anyone joining you – whether they’re family members of the human or animal kind!

Not Sure if You Should Apply?

Many candidates with great skills and experience second-guess themselves. The bar is high, but if this role excites you, apply! We’re here to help you succeed. Also, we're happy to learn about any specific accommodations you may need to fully engage in our recruitment process.

Wishing you all the best,
The Supercell Recruitment team

About Us

Lupa is building a category defining product the industry has never seen before.

We are the AI-native operating system for veterinary practices and pet parents, replacing the fragmented, clunky systems vets have tolerated for years with a single intelligent platform for scheduling, client communication, clinical documentation, and AI-driven care guidance. Practices run more efficiently, vets get back to doing what they love, and pet parents feel more connected to their animals health than ever.

The traction speaks for itself: one of Europe's top 100 AI startups with a team of 70 people, 10x growth in twelve months, the UK market leader, and now charging hard into the US and Europe. We have $25M in funding, 2.5M+ pets on the platform, and a buzzing HQ in Paddington, London.

This is a rare chance to join a rocket ship at exactly the right moment and we are looking for exceptional people to help us fly it.

In this role, you will:

  • Be Lupa's first in-house legal hire, building the legal function from scratch and owning everything from commercial contracts to regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions

  • Own and negotiate all commercial agreements including enterprise SaaS contracts, partner deals, vendor agreements, and everything in between, moving at the pace the business demands

  • Lead data privacy and security compliance across UK GDPR, EU GDPR, and US state privacy laws as we expand internationally

  • Navigate the regulatory landscape for AI-powered clinical tools in veterinary and adjacent healthcare markets across the UK, EU, and US

  • Support the board and leadership on corporate governance, equity matters, and future fundraising processes

  • Manage employment law across an increasingly international team including UK, US, and other jurisdictions as we scale

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure our AI features are built and deployed compliantly, from data handling to clinical liability

  • Own IP strategy, protecting what we build and making sure we are not infringing on what others have built

  • Build relationships with external counsel and manage those relationships commercially and strategically

Your background looks something like:

  • Qualified solicitor or barrister with 7+ years PQE. English and Welsh qualification essential, US bar admission a strong advantage

  • Significant experience in technology, SaaS, or digital health law, ideally with in-house experience at a high-growth startup or scale-up

  • Deep knowledge of data privacy law including UK/EU GDPR and experience operationalising compliance in a product-led company

  • Commercial contract experience at pace. You have negotiated complex enterprise deals and know how to move quickly without creating unnecessary risk

  • Exposure to regulatory frameworks for AI or health tech products (nice to have)

  • Experience supporting a fundraising process at Series A, B, or beyond (nice to have)

  • Background at a top-tier law firm before moving in-house (nice to have)

As a person, you:

  • Are a pragmatic, commercially minded lawyer. Your job is to help the business move fast safely, not to find reasons to slow things down

  • Are comfortable being the only lawyer in the room and making confident calls with incomplete information

  • Build trust quickly across a business, from engineers who need a quick data handling answer to the CEO who needs a board-ready governance opinion

  • Are genuinely excited by the intersection of AI, health tech, and regulation. This space is moving fast and you want to be at the front of it

  • Are excited to work in-person from our Paddington, London HQ

  • Value working with people who are kind, ambitious, and pragmatic

What does success look like in 6 months?

  • The legal function exists. Contracts are standardised, compliance frameworks are in place, and the business is no longer making it up as it goes

  • You are a trusted voice at the leadership table, pulled into strategic decisions early rather than brought in to review at the end

  • The US expansion has legal infrastructure behind it. Entity structure, contracts, employment, and privacy are all covered

About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the role

The Inference team builds and runs the systems that serve Mistral's models to the world.

We own the path from a trained model to a response on someone's screen. That includes the APIs and gateway that requests come through, routing and scheduling across our GPU fleet, and the capacity, deployment and operations work that keeps it all running.

Our work serves two groups. Customers need fast, reliable and cost-efficient inference as usage keeps growing. Our researchers rely on the same systems for evaluation, data generation and reinforcement learning, so what we build feeds directly into the next generation of models.

 

What You Will Do

As an Engineer on Inference, you'll build and run the services that sit between our users and our models. The work is close to the product and to the hardware, and the improvements you make show up quickly in latency, reliability, cost and how fast we can ship new models.

Experience with LLM inference is a plus, but it isn't a requirement. We're just as interested in strong Systems Engineers from other backgrounds who are keen to go deep on serving.

A few of the problems our teams work on:

  • Designing and evolving our inference APIs, so model capabilities like tool calling, structured outputs and new modalities are available to developers on launch day.

  • The backend services and gateway every request passes through, from authentication, streaming and rate limiting to usage metering, observability and end-to-end reliability.

  • Routing, load balancing and autoscaling across our clusters, so we absorb traffic spikes without wasting GPUs.

  • Faster, safer rollouts of new models and serving releases.

What We're Looking For

  • Have several years of experience shipping and running backend or distributed systems that serve real production traffic.

  • Write high-quality production code, and are comfortable using AI coding tools without compromising on it.

  • Care about performance and reliability, and enjoy making systems faster, cheaper and more robust.

  • Have led the design of significant systems, making the right trade-offs and seeing them through to production.

  • Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code review, design discussions and mentoring.

  • It’s a plus if you’ve shipped production backend services in Python or Go, or operated Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure at scale

  • Experience with LLM serving engines such as vLLM is a strong plus.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER

Catapult is building the future of sports performance technology, with a mission to Unleash the Potential of every athlete and team on earth. We don't just work in the sporting industry; we are actively changing it.  Since 2006, our solutions have been leading the way in sports performance software, science, and data, in a world where 1% can literally mean the difference between winning and losing.

We work with over 5,800 teams around the world, empowering coaches, managers and trainers in premier teams in the NFL, NBA, NHL, MLS, EPL, AFL, NRL, NCAA and more. We provide the information they need to optimize athletes' health, game-day readiness, and performance, as well as in-game tactics.  

Catapult is a sports technology company that empowers professional teams to make data-driven decisions. We deliver health, performance, video, and AI insights from the locker room to competitive environments, ensuring every decision is an opportunity to gain an advantage, sharpen performance, and build lasting success. 

WE WANT PEOPLE WHO ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT SOLVING HARD PROBLEMS

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build the Perch camera system, 

Based in London (hybrid), you will work across platform, perception, and ML systems. You will help us improve how we collect, process, and analyze performance data at scale, spanning from devices collecting real-time to backend services and ML infrastructure. All of which will have a direct impact on customers and their experiences with the product.

This role suits a strong generalist who has seen many parts of engineering. You might have worked on any of the following: high-throughput systems, computer vision, robotics, ML infrastructure, or other complex applications. Our ideal candidate brings strong engineering judgment, good technical range, and the ability to learn quickly.

You will be hands-on, working in Python and C++ on devices and services in use by our customers every day.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

  • Design and implement algorithms for 3D object tracking, segmentation, and motion recognition on embedded hardware.
  • Train and iterate on ML models — from dataset curation through training, evaluation, and deployment to edge devices.
  • Help bring ML, computer vision, or signal-processing systems into production with tight performance constraints
  • Build reliable application features and services that customers use in real environments.
  • Analyze production data to find system limits, product issues, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Collaborate closely with the embedded platform team on model optimization and inference performance, and with the applications team on how tracking data becomes product features.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience in production systems.
  • Strong skill in Python and backend engineering.
  • Working knowledge of C++ or a strong reason to be effective in performance-critical code.
  • Experience with data-intensive systems, distributed systems, parallel processing, or efficient data pipelines.
  • Exposure to ML, ML infrastructure, signal processing, real-time systems, computer vision, or related applied technical areas.
  • A track record of shipping reliable software, not only prototypes.
  • Strong debugging skills and the ability to find the root cause of complex system behavior.
  • Clear communication and good judgment when tradeoffs are not simple.
  • Curiosity, adaptability, and the desire to learn new technical areas.

Nice to have — and what would make you exceptional:

  • Experience with computer vision, depth cameras, pose estimation, tracking, or 3D data.
  • Experience with ML model deployment, feature pipelines, evaluation systems, or data quality tools.
  • Experience with streaming data, event systems, real-time processing, or low-latency applications.
  • Experience with numerical methods, signal processing, filtering, state estimation, or robotics.

WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE

  • In 6 months time, you understand the main systems, ship reliable changes, and help improve a meaningful data or product workflow. You give valuable technical input towards solving problems across backend, data, and perception systems.
  • In 12 months time, you have made a measurable impact on system reliability, product capability, or data quality. You own important parts of the architecture and help the team make better technical decisions.

WHY CATAPULT? 

  • We have amazing people. We promise you'll work with some of the most ambitious,  intelligent people in an exciting industry, and do some of the best work of your life.
  • We encourage our people to engage in constructive, open, and honest communication to make Catapult extraordinary. 
  • We work in a collaborative yet challenging environment to consistently improve our performance, which in turn impacts our customers' performance.
  • Our workforce spans more than 20 countries. You'll have the opportunity to work with people from multiple nationalities and cultures, and to build your global awareness.  
  • We value improvement and development. We are challenging ourselves to continuously grow and become a high-performance company. That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve.  There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.

Whether you're interested in sports or not, you'll have the satisfaction of knowing your work is supporting some of the most successful teams and athletes on the planet! 

Research shows that while men apply for jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalized groups tend only to apply when they check every box. So if you have what it takes, but don't meet every single point in our job ad, please still get in touch! We would love to have a chat and see if you could be a great addition to our team. We are building the future of sports performance. Our priority is to find the brightest talent who can add to our team culture, actively contribute, and be excited about what they do.

All offers of employment are subject to Catapult's positive prehire check. To find out more, please contact the Talent Partner for this role.

About DataCamp

DataCamp's mission is to empower everyone with the data and AI skills essential for 21st-century success. By providing practical, engaging learning experiences, DataCamp equips learners and organizations of all sizes to harness the power of data and AI. As a trusted partner to over 17 million learners and 6,000+ companies, including 80% of the Fortune 1000, DataCamp is leading the charge in addressing the critical data and AI skills shortage.

About the role

Research has consistently shown that one-on-one tutoring dramatically outperforms traditional classroom instruction—a finding known as Bloom's 2 Sigma Problem. Despite decades of awareness, no solution has successfully delivered personalized tutoring at scale. Until now.

We are building an AI tutoring system designed to emulate and eventually surpass the best human tutors. You will work on the core AI system that delivers real-time, adaptive learning experiences to learners. If you're excited about building the future of human learning, this role is for you. This role can be done remotely from anyone of the following; United Kingdom, Belgium, Portugal OR UAE

About you

At DataCamp, we seek individuals who embody our core values of data-driven decision-making, action, transparency, ownership, and customer focus. You thrive in a fast-paced, high-performing environment and are driven by a passion for making a meaningful impact. You're adaptable, embracing change and ambiguity with enthusiasm. Your initiative and entrepreneurial spirit push you beyond just meeting targets—you aim to understand the "why" behind our goals and take ownership to drive the business forward. You're a collaborative team player who values transparency and always seeks to improve and innovate. If this sounds like you, we encourage you to apply!

Responsibilities

  • Build and evolve the core AI tutoring system, including prompt architectures, agentic workflows, and real-time adaptive behaviors.
  • Run rigorous experimentation and evaluation, developing custom metrics and frameworks to measure learning effectiveness and improve model reliability.
  • Design and implement scalable, maintainable software, integrating AI capabilities with platform systems, content pipelines, and user experience components.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with educators, content creators, and product teams to translate pedagogical goals into technical solutions.
  • Prototype and productionize novel model interactions, leveraging emerging research and capabilities to advance the tutor's intelligence.
  • Ensure quality, safety, and observability through monitoring, testing, guardrails, and iterative refinement of model behavior.
  • Share knowledge and elevate teammates, contributing to a culture of clarity, simplicity, and continuous learning.

Qualifications

Technical

  • 1+ years building complex LLM-based systems, with strong prompt engineering intuition and experience designing agentic workflows.
  • Ability to design meaningful evaluation methods, including custom metrics and frameworks when off-the-shelf options fall short.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, architectural thinking, and fluency in Python; comfortable working with production infrastructure, cloud environments, and CI/CD.
  • Actively follows AI research and emerging capabilities, applying new ideas creatively to real problems.

Product & Pedagogy

  • Strong empathy for learners and content creators; able to translate pedagogical goals into system behavior and product decisions.
  • Ability to reason holistically across AI behavior, content structure, platform features, and user experience.
  • Familiarity with learning science or a desire to develop expertise.

Character & Collaboration

  • Drawn to difficult, ambiguous problems with no clear blueprint; persistent in exploring and refining solutions.
  • Preference for elegance and simplicity in system design.
  • Communicates clearly across mediums and enjoys mentoring and collaborating in small, high-ownership teams.

Why Datacamp? 

Joining DataCamp means becoming part of a dynamic, creative, and international start-up. Here are just a few of the reasons why you'll love being on our team:

  • Exciting challenges: Face new technical challenges daily, keeping your work engaging and rewarding.
  • Competitive compensation: We offer a competitive salary with attractive benefits.
  • Flexibility: Benefit from flexible working hours because the future is flexible! 
  • Continuous learning: Access a yearly learning budget for conferences & training to support your professional growth.
  • Global retreats: Participate in international company retreats, fostering a global team spirit.
  • Equipment: Yearly refreshment of your IT Equipment budget for your home working setup.
  • Amazing team: Collaborate with a truly exceptional team—seriously, we're awesome!

A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

Customers trust us when things go wrong. We're the software reliability platform built to investigate, respond to and prevent incidents. As a Commercial CSM, you're the partner to our mid-market engineering teams - getting them onboarded, embedded and expanding their usage, and maturing their incident management and reliability as they grow.

What that looks like day to day

Our Customer Success organisation is at the heart of incident.io. We're the team closest to our customers' hardest problems, and we're trusted to solve them. We believe in a customer-led product approach, working hand in hand with Product to uncover and address what each customer really needs. Our goal goes beyond satisfaction: we want to delight customers at every stage of their journey, and build long-term relationships grounded in trust, shared success and mutual growth.

You'll look after 70–80 Commercial customers: growth-oriented tech companies, mostly under 1,000 people, between $30k and $150k ARR each. Industry leaders like Vanta, Monday.com and Loom sit in this segment. Some are steady, some are scaling fast, and much of the job is knowing which is which, and what each one needs from you.

Most of your time goes to mid-market customers on our top-tier plan, where you're their dedicated CSM leading onboarding and adoption. You'll blend 1:1 time with scalable programmes to get teams to value quickly: best-practice sessions, end-user training, partnership and roadmap reviews. You'll also cover a subset of smaller customers in a low-touch capacity, leaning on usage data to spot risk and opportunity early.

Day to day, this is a high ownership role. You'll help customers navigate the product, unpick problems when they hit them, and keep everyone pointed at the outcomes their team actually cares about. You are responsible for proactively identifying expansion and upsell opportunities, and partnering with Sales and Expansion Account Managers to grow revenue within your accounts. Internally, you're the voice of the Commercial customer with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing and Support.

There's still a lot to build and a ton of opportunity for you to shape this segment. The Commercial motion works, but scaling and automating the customer journey is live work we're ramping up now - refining playbooks, automating the repeatable stuff, building the tooling and content that makes a portfolio this size easier to serve. We're AI-forward in how we approach it, so you'd be shaping this rather than inheriting it.

Who you are

  • You've carried a book of 40 to 100+ accounts and worked out how to be present across all of them without going quiet on half.

  • You've sold to, or supported, technical people, whether that's engineering teams, on-call rotations or developer tools. You can hold your own in a technical conversation without needing to escalate every one of them.

  • You've got commercial instincts. You spot the account that's about to double, you know what a growth signal looks like, and you know how to steer a renewal to a good outcome.

  • You know what scaled CS looks like when it's done well. Playbooks, one-to-many programs, AI-assisted workflows. You don't need to have built them from scratch, but you've worked around them enough to have opinions on what you'd do differently.

  • Half-built process doesn't rattle you. You'd rather fix the documentation than complain about it.

  • You actually like being in a room with customers, and you'll get on a plane for the right one.

Supporting you

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

  • Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover — we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

  • Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

  • First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

  • Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

  • Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

  • Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

  • Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

  • Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

Compensation: £85K – £118K • Offers Equity

  • London • £85K – £118K • Offers Equity

About us

Salience Labs is building an industry-defining approach to optical circuit switching for AI infrastructure, engineered for real latency reduction and cost savings. We're moving towards real-world deployment, and joining at this stage means genuine ownership over that next chapter, working alongside a highly technical team on one of the most consequential problems in AI infrastructure today.

The Role

As Finance Director at Salience Labs, you will own financial control, compliance and reporting across our UK, German and US entities, supporting our business strategy in a fast-paced, high-tech scale-up. Reporting to the CFO and working closely with cross-functional teams, you will lead the finance function and stay hands-on, equally comfortable running a close and building the scalable processes that improve it.

Financial control and reporting

  • Run the monthly consolidation across three entities: review trial balances, translate currencies, reconcile intercompany accounts and post eliminations.

  • Prepare group management accounts, Board materials and project-based reporting (actuals and cash use against budget), explaining the movements that matter to leadership.

  • Lead annual budgeting and quarterly reforecasting across all entities, tracking actuals against plan and highlighting key variances.

  • Develop and implement internal control policies and procedures.

Statutory, tax and compliance

  • Prepare UK GAAP statutory accounts and VAT returns, work with advisers on corporation tax, manage HMRC and Companies House deadlines, and coordinate the year-end audit.

  • Work with our German tax adviser (Steuerberater) on local VAT and tax filings, and reconcile the statutory books to group reporting.

  • Ensure US tax and statutory compliance with external advisers.

Payroll, cash and operations

  • Prepare and review payroll across entities, post payroll journals, and reconcile payroll liability, tax and benefit control accounts.

  • Manage cash flow and oversee day-to-day finance operations for the US and German entities, including cash balances, supplier payments and expenses.

  • Support vendor negotiations and maintain key financial relationships.

Inventory, costing and assets

  • Own month-end inventory reconciliations and cost of sales tracking. Work with operations and engineering to verify quantities and values for raw materials, WIP and finished goods (including stock held at third-party sites), and investigate manufacturing variances.

  • Maintain and reconcile fixed asset, depreciation and prepayment schedules across entities.

Grants, R&D and strategic projects

  • Monitor and report on grant, R&D and contract expenditure, including preparing and submitting grant reimbursement claims.

  • Contribute to strategic projects, including share option scheme management.

Systems and process improvement

  • Implement and optimise our finance systems, from defining requirements and testing workflows to supporting users through the first close after launch.

What we're looking for

  • ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent qualification, with a minimum of 10 years' post-qualification experience, including 5+ years in start-up or fast-growth environments.

  • Proven experience in financial controllership, personally preparing multi-currency group consolidations and UK statutory accounts, handling VAT returns and coordinating corporation tax filings, with UK payroll compliance and IFRS and/or GAAP knowledge.

  • Experience taking a finance system (accounting, expense or payroll) through implementation and its first close, including balance validation and workflow testing.

  • Experience managing inventory valuation, WIP or product costing in a hardware or manufacturing business.

  • Strong attention to detail, with clean reconciliations, accurate intercompany balances and reliable inventory figures.

  • A proactive mindset, anticipating process gaps and upcoming tax or audit deadlines early.

  • Practical problem-solving: digging into the root cause of variances across manufacturing costs and cross-border accounting rather than simply flagging them.

  • Composure and sound judgement in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift.

  • Clear communication, translating complex financial movements and cost drivers into plain English for leadership, engineering and operations.

Even better if you

  • Are familiar with financial regulations and practices in Germany and the US.

  • Have experience in fabless manufacturing or high-tech industries such as semiconductors.

  • Have a track record of leading software selection and implementation projects.

  • Have leadership skills to drive innovation and growth within the finance function.

Senior Data Protection Engineer (Backup & Cyber Resilience)

Location: Windsor, UK

Introduction

We’re hiring a Senior Data Protection Engineer to join a global hosting and managed services team. The team runs business-critical, highly regulated systems for organisations around the world, many of them in healthcare, where losing data or failing to recover it is not an option.

This is a senior role with real influence. You’ll own the enterprise backup and recovery platform across all regions. You’ll set the standards for how data is protected, retained and restored, and you’ll show, with evidence, that recovery targets are met. You’ll also help shape where data protection services go next, at a time when cyber resilience matters more than ever.

Responsibilities & Tasks

  • Run the platform globally. Lead the engineering, administration and continuous improvement of an enterprise Rubrik environment. This covers configuration, upgrades, capacity planning, health monitoring, security hardening and lifecycle management.

  • Set the rules. Design and enforce global protection policies, including SLA tiers, retention, archiving, replication, immutability, encryption and access controls.

  • Turn requirements into protection. Convert business, regulatory, contractual and risk needs into clear protection tiers, RPO and RTO targets, and practical operating procedures.

  • Keep coverage complete. Bring new workloads into the service and keep protection accurate across on-premises, cloud, virtualised, database and application environments.

  • Keep operations healthy. Monitor backup, replication, archiving and restore activity. Fix failed jobs, capacity pressure, performance issues and policy exceptions before they become risks.

  • Prove that recovery works. Plan and run restore tests, disaster recovery exercises and readiness reviews, and keep the evidence that recovery targets and controls are met.

  • Strengthen cyber resilience. Work with security and incident response teams on ransomware readiness, anomaly investigations, clean-recovery planning and privileged-access controls.

  • Build strong governance. Write the runbooks, standards and procedures that define good practice, and help regions and technology teams adopt them consistently.

  • Lead when it counts. Take technical ownership during incidents and service disruptions, and drive root cause analysis and lasting corrective actions.

  • Automate. Use APIs, scripting and orchestration tools to automate routine operations, compliance checks, reporting and workflows.

  • Report clearly. Give regular insight into protection coverage, recoverability, compliance, capacity, platform risk and operational performance.

  • Work across teams. Partner closely with infrastructure, cloud, database, application, security, risk and business continuity colleagues, and take part in a shared on-call rota for critical production services.

Requirements & Qualifications

Essential:

  • A solid track record of engineering and running enterprise-scale backup, recovery and data protection services

  • Extensive hands-on production experience with Rubrik

  • A current Rubrik Certified System Administrator (RCSA) certification

  • Experience designing and rolling out data protection policies, standards and operating models across multiple regions

  • A strong grasp of retention, immutability, encryption, access control, RPO and RTO, and recovery validation

  • Hands-on involvement in disaster recovery, cyber recovery or ransomware-resilience initiatives

  • Strong troubleshooting skills, and familiarity with incident, change and problem management processes

  • Experience supporting production services in a 24x7 or on-call environment

Benefits & Culture

  • Global reach and visible impact: Your work will directly protect critical services, including healthcare systems that clinicians and care providers rely on every day.

  • Real ownership: You’ll have a strong voice in policy design, retention strategy, cyber resilience, automation and the long-term direction of the service.

  • Collaborative environment: You’ll join experienced engineers and architects who value shared ownership, operational excellence and openly sharing knowledge.

  • Growth and development: You’ll keep developing your skills on an enterprise-grade platform, with support for certifications and continuous learning.

  • Competitive rewards: The package includes market-aligned pay and comprehensive benefits that reflect a senior technical role.

If you want to make data protection dependable at a global scale, we’d love to hear from you.

At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.

We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.

With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?

About the role

We are looking for a sales engineer to join our sales team and drive the frontline of industrial decarbonisation.

This role bridges the technical and commercial worlds. You'll need interpersonal and technical skills to build relationships with process engineers in cement plants and understand their challenges. Analytical skills will be essential to delve deep into complex plant data and work out how Gigaton's AI products can solve their most critical issues.

Building on that, you'll need strategic thinking and commercial awareness to turn your findings into concise, compelling proposals for decision-makers at our customers, from the C-suite down.

Ultimately, you'll build clarity from uncertainty, making sure we agree a shared roadmap with our customers that puts our solutions on track for significant real-world benefits before a contract is signed.

Over time, you’ll help us evolve our sales approach and shape the product by feeding insights and needs from the plant back to the product team, building the foundation for scaling across industries.

Your main responsibilities

  • Be the technical expert on sales calls and visits with cement plants.

  • Build trust with process engineers and plant teams by understanding their specific plant issues and linking them to how we can help.

  • Analyse plant data to identify and evaluate opportunities, then use this analysis to create compelling sales proposals.

  • Lead technical discovery and identify early when a plant does not meet our ICP (ideal customer profile) criteria.

  • Make sure relationships and plant understanding are handed over successfully to the deployment team.

  • Act as a feedback loop into Gigaton’s product and machine learning teams, providing field insights that help shape our product roadmap.

  • Develop and iterate the pre-sales technical process, making it more impactful and more automated each time.

  • Travel to plants and conferences, around one week per month, to understand customer environments and explain the product.

What a great fit looks like

  • Exposure to physical sciences, controls, or heavy industry, such as cement, steel, energy, manufacturing, or similar.

  • Strong analytical skills and an outcome-oriented mindset. You can dig into industrial data, identify root causes, generate potential solutions, and explain their value in dollars and tonnes of CO2.

  • Excellent communication skills. You can build credibility and trust in complex industrial environments with both engineers and board-level stakeholders.

  • Comfortable being the technical voice in the conversation, presenting to senior plant leaders and operators, handling objections, and being challenged on your findings by people who have run kilns for 30 years.

  • Naturally curious and keen to learn about the industry, the technology, and each individual plant. You want to understand the root cause behind every question and objection so you can solve the right problem.

  • Confident in ambiguity and able to field very specific technical questions without getting flustered. You know when you can give your understanding, when you need to go and find the answer, and how to maintain customer confidence in both situations.

  • Willingness to travel regularly.

You’ll excel if

  • You build trust easily. You can connect with plant engineers, listen deeply, and align solutions to their priorities.

  • You’d rather diagnose than pitch. Your first instinct in a plant is to ask a better question, not to open the deck.

  • You thrive in dynamic environments. Fast-paced, ambiguous settings excite you, and you’re motivated by high-impact, mission-driven work.

  • You have experience working in heavy industry, particularly cement, steel, energy, heavy manufacturing, or similar.

Success in This Role Means

  • Plants say yes because the technical case is clear. You build customer confidence that Gigaton can deliver high ROI, helping us hit our revenue goals without losing deals because customers don’t understand or believe in our product and capabilities.

  • Deployments are set up to succeed. We haven’t overpromised to sign a contract, and our pre-contract analysis holds up once the system is live.

  • Process engineers trust and rely on you as a partner in solving problems.

  • Deals don’t stall waiting on a technical answer. Objections get handled quickly, and customers get the answers they need in good time.

    💡 You are not expected to check every box, and we’d love to hear from you even if your experience isn’t an exact match.

    We’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change. Our people come from all walks of life, with different countries, cultures, and experiences, and we think that’s one of our biggest strengths.

    We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and celebrated. No matter your background, if you’re excited by what we do, we want to hear from you.

The interview process

  1. Talent Partner Screen Call: Meet our talent partner and learn more about Gigaton and the role.

  2. Hiring Manager Screen: Meet our VP of Sales and discuss if this role is a good fit for you.

  3. Technical Onsite (completed on the same day):

    1. Technical interview

    2. Data analysis & presentation

  4. Operating Principles Interview: Understand how we work and whether Gigaton and you are a good fit for each other.

  5. Meet with the CEO: Every new potential hire meets Josh.

We believe hiring is a two-way process. Just as we’ll reference-check candidates before making a final offer, we encourage you to reference-check us by chatting to team members you haven’t yet met. Ask anything. We’ll answer with Concrete Honesty.

Once interviews are done, we’ll move quickly to a decision, and we’re always happy to give feedback at any stage.

In return for your hard work, we’ll give you

📈 Equity in the company: When we win, you win. You’ll get share options, so you’re part of our journey from the inside.

🕰️ Flexible working We trust you to know how and when you work best and to work that out with your team.

🌴 30 days of holiday (plus bank holidays). Rest is productive. Take the time you need to recharge

🪙 A generous pension scheme. We’re planning for the future in more ways than one.

Our Operating Principles

↗️ Go Gig or Go Home: High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires.

🏭 Concrete Honesty: Be honest. As concrete forms the foundation of our world, genuine honesty and transparency are the bedrock of our culture.

🦾 Autonomous Ownership: High agency, high ownership. We build systems that take control and make things better. We do the same: see it, own it, drive it.

😄 Cement it with Kindness & Fun: Have fun, be kind. We're here to extend Earth's life, but ours is still limited. We want to enjoy the ride. To see these in full, go to Gigaton’s Operating Principles Notion page.

Compensation: £60K – £85K

Wayve’s Technical Operations function is the critical bridge between Product, Engineering, and Operations. We thrive in dynamic, high-growth environments, turning complex technical strategies into actionable field operations that set the standard for autonomy at scale.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

 

You’ll stand up and run technical operations in new markets—planning data collection campaigns, preparing vehicles and operators for launch, and running live robotaxi services with our ridehail partners. Your work will build the feedback loops that convert on-road data, operator insights, and service metrics into continuous product enhancements, demonstrating improvements through live operations. You’ll drive the pace and reliability required to deliver commercial services where customer experience and operational reliability are measured daily.

  • Market launch readiness: Turn program plans into clear, actionable launch plans by market, covering vehicle commissioning, operator readiness, route and ODD validation, and safety sign-offs. Lead go/no-go reviews across multiple regions.

  • Performance reporting: Own weekly product performance reporting—including autonomy time, pickups/drop-offs, km driven, and safety events—and turn trends into priority actions for Operations, Engineering, and Product.

  • Field-to-model feedback loops: Be the link between on-road operations and model, product, and research teams. Triage on-road events, route insights, and design targeted testing to close data gaps.

  • Scaling the playbook: Improve processes, SOPs, and tooling so each new market launches faster and more safely.

 

🙌 You should apply if

 

Essential:

Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

 

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

 

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

 

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

 

Initial call / recruiter screen - 30 mins

 

Competency Interviews - 45 mins

 

Deep-dive technical interviews - Case Study Presentation - 1 hour

 

Final interview: mission & values alignment - 30 mins

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.
